candidates.tagline: Coca-Cola's rebrand brief: 'More Coca-Cola.' The internet: 'That's a Marlboro.'
candidates.story: On July 20, 2026 Coca-Cola launched a global visual identity refresh — its new 'Better With' serif typeface is so similar to Marlboro's font that social media users immediately posted side-by-side comparisons, calling it the 'fridge cigarette' rebrand; simultaneously, swapping from black to white lettering makes Coke Zero nearly indistinguishable from regular Coke, alarming diabetics who rely on the colour difference.
candidates.why_funny: The world's most iconic drink brand paid a branding agency millions to look 'more Coca-Cola' and accidentally arrived at 'more Marlboro' — while also making the safe-for-diabetics version of their drink invisible on the shelf.
candidates.alt: New 2026 Coca-Cola global brand refresh showing the redesigned red-and-white cans and bottles with the updated tall serif typeface that internet users compare to Marlboro cigarette packaging

candidates.tagline: Elon promised 250,000 Cybertrucks a year. It's outsold by a 1958 Ford.
candidates.story: Sales data published July 22, 2026 shows the Tesla Cybertruck — pre-reserved by over 2 million people and predicted by Elon Musk to sell 250,000+ units in its first year — registered just 38,965 units in 2024, 20,237 in 2025, and 7,133 through May 2026; Jalopnik and Bloomberg both declared it now sells at a pace worse than the Ford Edsel, the car that has been shorthand for 'legendary automotive disaster' since 1958.
candidates.why_funny: The most pre-ordered vehicle in the history of the automobile turned out to sell slower than the universally-mocked car from the Eisenhower administration that became the dictionary definition of a flop.
candidates.alt: A silver stainless-steel Tesla Cybertruck parked on a residential street corner in Greenwich, its distinctive angular wedge-shaped body gleaming in daylight
